grandparents_cupboard.reason: Eggs, mushrooms, spring onions, cheddar, olive oil, parsley and wholemeal bread are all ordinary kitchen foods with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at Tesco or any mainstream supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only an ovenproof frying pan, a bowl, a whisk and a grater, and starting a frittata on the hob then finishing it in the oven is well within a confident beginner's reach.

works.reason: Eight eggs, 250g mushrooms, a bunch of spring onions and 75g cheddar make a sensible frittata for four, and a gentle hob start followed by 10 to 12 minutes at 200°C will set it without drying it out.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes covers slicing the mushrooms and spring onions, grating, whisking and the hob stage, and 15 minutes cooking matches the bake plus toast, which is believable at a standard pace.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including the parsley and the bread served as toast, is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm egg breakfast suits mid-March, and a whole bunch of spring onions is cooked into the frittata and scattered over the top, so they are central rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English that a neighbour would follow easily.

hearty_healthy.reason: Eggs, vegetables, cheese and wholemeal toast make a filling, real-food breakfast a family would happily eat again.
